subject.title: [Feature]: Add a real workspace-only Restricted onboarding preset

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-run Restricted host-access preset whose label promises workspace-only OpenClaw file tools and no native host execution, while unavailable provider-native restrictions fail closed?
rationale: This chooses a durable user-facing security posture, its acceptable provider fallback behavior, and the scope of the onboarding promise; source-level implementation cannot safely decide those product and compatibility boundaries.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded Restricted preset
options.body: Approve the proposed host-owned preset contract, require provider-specific restricted-surface proof, and fail closed for providers that cannot honor it.

options.title: Narrow to terminology only
options.body: Rename the discovery-consent choice without adding a host-access preset, avoiding a new security promise but leaving restricted execution as advanced configuration.

options.title: Defer until isolation architecture is defined
options.body: Keep the current setup flow while maintainers define whether Restricted should mean policy-only limitation or stronger sandbox/OS isolation.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded Restricted preset
recommendation.body: Approve the proposed host-owned preset contract, require provider-specific restricted-surface proof, and fail closed for providers that cannot honor it.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the concrete contract and tradeoffs, and can refine the proposal with maintainer direction.
